Footnote

The results are estimates of learners’ ability. They come from samples of learners that represent the country and each state, and sampling weights are applied. The number of learners assessed is the size of the sample. It is not the number of learners in Nigeria, and the estimates describe all learners in the grade.

Groups with fewer than 100 learners assessed are marked for caution. Groups with fewer than 30 learners are not shown. Proficiency levels come from IRT-scaled ability estimates.

  1. The cut points for 2022 tests are 400 to 449 for below partially meets, 450 to 499 for partially meets, 500 to 549 for meets, and 550 to 600 for exceeds.
  2. The cut points for 2026 tests will be added when the 2026 results are loaded.

NALABE 2022 results follow the analysis behind the 2022 report. They will be updated when the 2022 results are placed on the 2026 scale. Basic science and technology and social studies were assessed in Primary 5 and Junior Secondary 2 only.
